subject: Feature-basket restructure & pilot seat uplift options
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@luminahealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumina Health Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — mid-pilot uplift and preserving Advanced Routing feature?

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks good and the team liked the inference cost breakdown. We've run an internal eval (attached) and have two immediate packaging questions as we scope a 3-month pilot:

1) We may need to temporarily increase pilot capacity (seat uplift) for 6 weeks to support a simulation run. How does Redwood handle a temporary tier uplift mid-pilot? Is there a way to get credits or prorated billing rather than a full tier commit?

2) The "Advanced Routing" feature is mission-critical for us. If we move to a lower tier after pilot, can we keep that feature toggled on as an add-on, and how would pricing look?

We're trying to avoid a large up-front commitment but want a clear path to a predictable production contract if the pilot succeeds. Can you outline 1-2 pragmatic options with rough pricing ranges and any discount possibilities?

Attached: Lumina_Eval_Report_Q1.pdf

Best,
Amit Shah
Director of Product, Lumina Health
amit@luminahealth.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@luminahealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — mid-pilot uplift and preserving Advanced Routing feature?

Hi Amit — thanks for the detail and the eval report (quick read, looks solid). Short answers up-front and two pragmatic paths below. Happy to hop on 20 minutes tomorrow to walk through numbers.

Quick summary:
- Temporary uplift: supported with prorated billing + pilot credit option (see Option A).
- Feature hold: Advanced Routing can be retained as an add-on after downgrade; price depends on throughput and KV cache retention SLA.

Option A — Low-commit pilot-friendly
- 3-month pilot; allow a one-time 6-week seat uplift. Uplift billed prorated at list, but we apply a pilot credit to offset up to 30% of uplift token costs for the first month.
- Advanced Routing available as add-on at 40% of the standard add-on rate during pilot, 100% post-pilot unless you commit to a 12-month term.
- No up-front Dedicated commit required.

Option B — Predictable production-lean
- Commit to 12 months (Reserved capacity) after pilot and we provide a structured discount: standard 15% off list for seat/throughput, plus a one-time onboarding credit equal to one week's baseline usage.
- Advanced Routing included in the Reserved SKU at a 20% uplift over base tier, and can be grandfathered for 6 months if you reduce capacity mid-term.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick call to confirm expected peak concurrency and desired retention for KV cache (that drives price on Advanced Routing).
2) I’ll send a short amendment with both options and the associated approx. numbers.

Putting Kimberly (sales lead) and Priya (solutions) on cc to prepare numbers and the draft amendment.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Feature-basket restructure & pilot seat uplift options (internal)

Internal note — negotiation play and numbers to prepare before we reply formally to Amit: 

- Baseline assumption: pilot baseline = 20 seats equivalent (they can spike to ~60 during the sim). Confirm with Amit asap.
- Recommended commercial offer:
  * Pilot path: keep Sean's pilot credit language but cap credits to first 30 days of uplift usage (clearly defined). Offer 25% uplift credit rather than 30% if they ask — leaves room.
  * Commitment path: 12-month Reserved with 15% off seat+token list; include onboarding credit equal to 1 week baseline usage. If they sign a PO within 21 days of pilot end, increase discount to 18%.
  * Advanced Routing handling: make it an explicit add-on code (AR-PLUS). Price AR-PLUS at 35% of base throughput cost for pilot; if they convert to Reserved and commit to baseline capacity >= 80% of pilot peak, move AR-PLUS into the Reserved SKU at a 20% uplift.
  * Contract language: add a 90-day grandfather clause for AR-PLUS on downgrade (helps procurement).

I've attached a short amendment (proposed_amendment_v2.docx) with the above clauses + fields for seat counts and desired KV cache retention SLA.

I'll prepare two short pricing tables (Pilot vs Reserved) with a numeric example (20 baseline -> 60 spike) and send to Sean to include in the external email.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Hi Amit — following up with concrete options and the materials Kimberly prepared. Apologies for the slightly longer message, I wanted to be explicit so procurement has something to review.

Option 1 — Pilot-first (no long-term commit)- 3-month pilot, baseline 20 seats equivalent, one-time 6-week spike permitted up to 60 seats. Uplift billed prorated at list price; Redwood applies a pilot uplift credit that reduces billed uplift token costs by up to 25% for the first 30 days of uplift usage.- Advanced Routing (AR-PLUS) as an add-on: during pilot priced at 35% of base throughput cost; included functionality: region routing, KV cache persist for 24 hours, and prioritized scheduling.

Option 2 — Pilot -> Reserved (predictable production)- If Lumina commits to a 12-month Reserved contract within 21 days after pilot, we offer 15% off seat/token list and a one-time onboarding credit equal to one week of baseline usage. We will fold AR-PLUS into the Reserved SKU at a 20% uplift over base, and provide a 90-day grandfather clause on downgrade for AR-PLUS. If you execute PO within 21 days we can extend discount to 18%.

Attachments: 1) Lumina_Eval_Report_Q1.pdf (your upload) 2) proposed_amendment_v2.docx (our draft amendment with fields to populate).

If this looks reasonable, next steps:
- Confirm expected baseline and peak seat numbers (20 / 60?) and KV cache retention target.
- I'll open a HubSpot deal stage entry and attach the draft; if agreeable I'll create a DocuSign packet next week. HubSpot ref: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DEAL-78934-LH

Available times for a 20-minute call tomorrow: 10:00am PT or 2:30pm PT. Which works for you?

Best,
